title: Judgment Recovery — Operator Companion Workbook
subtitle: 6 Printable Operator Worksheets for Commercial Judgment Underwriting, Recovery Economics, Attorney-Led Enforcement, Lawful Outreach, Deadline Automation, and Small-Team Launch Readiness

worksheets.title: Opportunity Underwriting and Counterparty Qualification
worksheets.purpose: Turn a judgment referral into an evidence-backed acquisition decision before committing investigation cash or promising enforcement. Separate creditor authority, debtor identity, enforceability, asset ownership, and priority so an attractive face amount cannot conceal an insolvent counterparty or an unusable enforcement path.
instructions: Choose one commercial judgment and assemble the entered judgment, docket, underlying transaction documents, payment history, and creditor identity records. Label each document with its retrieval date, source, and reviewer rather than treating a referral spreadsheet as evidence.

Map the actual judgment debtor to entity registrations and independently supported identifiers. Distinguish affiliates, guarantors, trade names, and owners; shared addresses or similar names do not make another person's property available to satisfy this judgment.

Have retained counsel identify the governing enforcement jurisdiction, current enforceability, service issues, renewal dates, and bankruptcy exposure. Record unresolved questions as specific research assignments with owners and dates, and exclude dependent actions until those questions are resolved.

Build an asset-level recovery waterfall using supported ownership, senior claims, exemptions, liquidation discounts, and execution costs. Apply uncertainty to the collectible pool rather than multiplying the judgment balance by an optimistic success percentage without an identified payment source.

Approve, defer, or reject the referral using written evidence thresholds and a capped investigation budget. Record the reason, next evidence request, responsible reviewer, and expiration date so stale underwriting cannot silently become authorization for enforcement spending.

fields.name: Commercial vertical and transaction classification
fields.prompt: Identify the originating transaction, debtor form, creditor segment, and proposed recovery service. Explain which documents establish business purpose and which facts could instead introduce consumer debt, personal liability, or specialist handling requirements.
fields.example: Target California equipment lessors holding judgments against operating limited liability companies. Sample case JR-001 concerns unpaid warehouse forklift leases, supported by an LLC lease and business invoices. A separate individual guaranty receives its own review; the operator does not assume every related obligation shares the same classification.

fields.name: Judgment identity and independently reconciled balance
fields.prompt: Record the court, case identifier, entered debtor name, judgment date, principal, allowed additions, interest method, and credited payments. Distinguish the enforceable claim balance from recognized service revenue and from any preliminary recovery estimate.
fields.example: Training case JR-001 uses a $120,000 commercial judgment entered January 2, 2026, with no credited payments or added costs. At an assumed applicable 10% simple rate, exactly 90 elapsed days produce $2,958.90 interest using 365 days. The resulting $122,958.90 claim is not operator revenue.

fields.name: Creditor authority and chain of ownership
fields.prompt: Identify who presently owns the judgment and who can engage the operator, instruct counsel, accept settlements, and receive distributions. List every assignment and required filing, and specify the evidence needed to resolve missing or inconsistent authority.
fields.example: The original lessor supplies its executed engagement, officer authorization, and judgment copy. No assignment is assumed. If the judgment is transferred, counsel verifies the complete chain and the acknowledgment required by California Code of Civil Procedure section 673 before relying on assignee enforcement authority.

fields.name: Debtor identity and ownership separation
fields.prompt: Match the named debtor to authoritative entity records and transaction documents. Record identifiers, status, locations, and exclusions while explaining how the team will prevent affiliate assets, personal accounts, or similarly named businesses from entering the recovery pool.
fields.example: JR-001 names Harbor Industrial Leasing Customer LLC in this training example. Its registration number and lease address match the judgment. Harbor Industrial Holdings LLC occupies the same building but is not a judgment debtor. Its real estate remains excluded unless counsel establishes a separate lawful basis.

fields.name: Enforceability and deadline evidence
fields.prompt: Document finality, appeal status, stays, service concerns, judgment age, and renewal requirements. Name the jurisdictional rule, source document, attorney reviewer, and next verification date rather than treating a docket entry as conclusive proof of enforceability.
fields.example: Counsel checks California Code of Civil Procedure sections 683.020 and 683.110 through 683.220 for the commercial judgment's enforcement and renewal framework. The tracker records the entered date, any renewal, and early review reminders. A pending motion or stay requires an explicit disposition before dependent activity resumes.

fields.name: Asset evidence and realizable value
fields.prompt: List each potential payment source with ownership evidence, valuation date, liquidity discount, location, and lawful discovery method. Separate verified assets from investigation leads and explain what must happen before a lead supports an execution budget.
fields.example: A commercial equipment appraisal supports $100,000 gross resale value for debtor-owned machinery. A 20% forced-sale discount reduces the working value to $80,000. A reported bank relationship remains only a lead until counsel obtains appropriate process; no employee seeks account details through impersonation or unauthorized access.

fields.name: Lien priority and residual recovery waterfall
fields.prompt: Calculate the amount available after senior interests, legally applicable protections, sale expenses, and competing claims. Explain how searches, payoff evidence, and counsel's priority analysis support the calculation and where unresolved claims change the result.
fields.example: The $80,000 discounted machinery value is reduced by a documented $30,000 senior secured payoff and $10,000 estimated sale and execution costs, leaving $40,000 for this judgment. Counsel applies the relevant enacted UCC provisions, including section 9-317 where applicable, rather than treating search order as lien priority.

fields.name: Bankruptcy and solvency assessment
fields.prompt: Record bankruptcy searches, entity condition, operating cash indicators, pending insolvency proceedings, and search limitations. Explain how new filing information reaches counsel and which activities pause while applicability of a stay or discharge is assessed.
fields.example: The researcher checks PACER using verified entity identifiers and records the search time and coverage. A new petition triggers an immediate enforcement hold and counsel review under 11 U.S.C. section 362. A negative search supports only that search's scope; it does not establish solvency or future collectibility.

fields.name: Counterparty qualification and spending mandate
fields.prompt: Define creditor document obligations, approved investigation spending, settlement authority, counsel engagement, reporting frequency, and termination mechanics. Identify who bears unrecovered costs and prohibit staff from expanding the mandate through informal messages or verbal assumptions.
fields.example: The creditor authorizes a $750 initial review and requires written consent for cumulative outside spending above $2,500. Counsel alone handles legal filings. Settlements below $35,000 require creditor authorization, and every settlement remains subject to the agreement's documented authority. The operator reports activity every 30 days.

fields.name: Underwriting disposition and decision expiry
fields.prompt: Select an evidence-based disposition and state the collectible pool, fee opportunity, unresolved defects, investigation ceiling, and decision expiry. Explain precisely what new evidence would change the decision and who can authorize that change.
fields.example: JR-001 is conditionally accepted for investigation, not immediate execution. The supported pool is $40,000 and the illustrative 35% fee opportunity is $14,000. Release of the next $1,000 requires a current secured payoff and counsel's enforcement plan. The underwriting decision expires after 30 days without refreshed evidence.

worksheets.completion_gate: The case owner and retained attorney have documented authority, enforceability, bankruptcy screening, asset ownership, priority, and a capped next step; unresolved evidence cannot support execution spending or an assertion of collectible value.

worksheets.title: Unit Economics, Defect Reserve, and Working-Capital Float
worksheets.purpose: Translate recoveries into earned service fees, modeled operating costs, and unrestricted cash needs. Reconcile every scenario to the canonical scorecard while keeping creditor principal, client cash, reimbursable advances, expected losses, and owner profit in separate analytical categories.
instructions: Start with the contractual fee base and recognition event, then derive gross service revenue from actual collection assumptions. Keep judgment balances and client distributions outside revenue, and show separately whether enforcement costs reduce the contractual fee base.

Reproduce the Conservative, Base, and Scaled annual scorecard exactly before adding sensitivity cases. Assign operating costs to mutually exclusive buckets, and distinguish these illustrative budget allocations from verified historical results or accounting policy conclusions.

Estimate scrub failures and unrecovered advances using explicit case counts, probabilities, and dollar exposures. Separate recognition of an expected cost from its cash payment so the same enforcement loss does not appear twice in either calculation.

Build a weekly unrestricted cash schedule covering delayed recoveries, outside counsel deposits, research invoices, and routine overhead. Exclude client balances and restricted funds from available liquidity even when those amounts sit in accounts the operator can view.

Stress the model for fewer successful matters, longer collection timelines, and cost overruns. Record a specific spending response and funded runway requirement; a modeled fee pipeline is not a substitute for cash during the six-to-twenty-four-month first-deal window.

fields.name: Contractual fee base and revenue recognition
fields.prompt: Define when a recovery fee becomes earned and measurable, which receipts enter the calculation, and how reversals or refunds are handled. Explain the difference between signed mandates, judgment principal, cleared recoveries, and recognized operator revenue.
fields.example: The planning contract earns 35% of cleared recoveries without deducting separately authorized enforcement expenses from the fee base. A $40,000 collected payment therefore supports a $14,000 fee and $26,000 creditor allocation before separate reimbursements. A signed $120,000 judgment mandate alone produces zero earned fees.

fields.name: Conservative annual scorecard reconciliation
fields.prompt: Reproduce the Conservative revenue, margin, owner net profit, and staffing exactly. Allocate the implied total cost across distinct operating categories, and show the collection volume required under the illustrative contractual fee percentage.
fields.example: Conservative recognized service fees are $60,000; modeled costs are $48,000, leaving $12,000 annual owner net profit at 20%. Staffing is 1 FT plus 3 C. Costs comprise $24,000 recurring overhead, $12,000 enforcement, $8,000 incremental contractors, and $4,000 expected losses. At 35%, required recoveries approximate $171,428.57.

fields.name: Base annual scorecard reconciliation
fields.prompt: Reproduce the Base revenue, margin, owner net profit, and team without substituting client recoveries for fees. Show a collection-level bridge and a complete cost allocation whose sum equals the scorecard's implied operating expense.
fields.example: Base assumes 20 successful matters collecting $40,000 each: $800,000 recoveries generate $280,000 fees at 35%. Costs of $196,000 comprise $96,000 recurring overhead, $60,000 enforcement, $20,000 incremental contractors, and $20,000 expected losses. Annual owner net profit is $84,000 at 30.0%, with 1 FT plus 3 C.

fields.name: Scaled small-team annual reconciliation
fields.prompt: Reproduce the Scaled revenue, margin, owner net profit, and six-person team exactly. Explain the implied recoveries and cost structure while distinguishing recurring monthly overhead from variable enforcement spending and separately modeled losses.
fields.example: Scaled recognized fees are $500,000 against $300,000 costs, yielding $200,000 annual owner net profit at 40%. Staffing is 2 FT plus 4 C, totaling six people. Costs are $144,000 recurring overhead, $96,000 enforcement, $40,000 incremental contractors, and $20,000 expected losses; 35% fees imply approximately $1,428,571.43 recoveries.

fields.name: Per-matter contribution and portfolio burden
fields.prompt: Calculate the contribution from one successful matter before shared overhead, then allocate unsuccessful-case spending and portfolio losses. State which costs are incremental and which staffing commitments already belong in recurring overhead.
fields.example: A Base success produces $14,000 fees, less $3,000 enforcement and $1,000 incremental contractor cost, leaving $10,000 before shared overhead and risk costs. Twenty successes produce $200,000; subtracting $96,000 overhead and $20,000 expected losses yields $84,000. Core contractor retainers already included in overhead are not charged again.

fields.name: Scrub defects and expected-loss reserve
fields.prompt: Estimate intake rejection rates and unrecovered spending from identified defects, then connect them to the annual cost model. Distinguish an internal budgeting allowance from accounting treatment and prohibit duplicate recognition when estimated losses become actual expenditures.
fields.example: From 50 reviewed referrals, 10 fail authority or collectibility checks at $200 each, producing $2,000 scrub costs. Six failed investigations averaging $3,000 add $18,000, completing the Base $20,000 risk budget. These losses are separate from successful-case enforcement costs; the accountant determines recognition and reconciles estimates against actual spending.

fields.name: Startup capital and unrestricted cash waterfall
fields.prompt: Build a dated cash bridge from contributed capital through setup, recurring spending, case deposits, and expected receipts. Identify the minimum operating balance and funding shortfall without borrowing client money or treating projected fees as collected cash.
fields.example: Opening unrestricted capital of $50,000 pays $10,000 setup, three months of $8,000 recurring overhead, and $15,000 case advances, leaving $1,000 before recoveries. A $12,000 minimum requires another $11,000, making the funded opening requirement $61,000. This fits the $10,000–$75,000 startup range but funds only this specified period.

fields.name: Cost reimbursement and creditor distribution
fields.prompt: Describe whether approved advances are recoverable from collections, billed independently, or absorbed by the operator. Calculate a sample distribution under the actual contract and distinguish agency reimbursements from service fees subject to the accountant's revenue policy.
fields.example: For a $40,000 cleared recovery, the agreement allocates $14,000 to fees and $26,000 to the creditor before a separately authorized $2,000 advance reimbursement. Cash distribution is $24,000 creditor, $14,000 fee, and $2,000 reimbursement. The reimbursement clears an advance receivable under this illustrative agency treatment; it is not another contingency fee.

fields.name: Delay and insolvency sensitivity
fields.prompt: Quantify a downside case separately from the canonical scenarios. Change success count, timing, and direct spending explicitly, then calculate profit and cash implications without quietly replacing the published Base assumptions.
fields.example: A stress case with 15 rather than 20 successes generates $210,000 fees. Using $96,000 overhead, $45,000 successful-case enforcement, $15,000 incremental contractors, and $20,000 losses leaves $34,000 profit. A further three-month cash delay requires $24,000 overhead funding before additional advances. The canonical Base remains $280,000 revenue and $84,000 profit.

fields.name: Economic decision and runway threshold
fields.prompt: State the minimum contribution, maximum exposed cash, monthly spending limit, and funding evidence required before accepting additional matters. Reconcile the short launch budget with the longer expected first-deal timing and record the response to insufficient runway.
fields.example: Accept additional matters only with positive documented contribution, a funded $12,000 cash floor, and creditor-approved advances. Planning ranges remain $2,000–$12,000 monthly recurring opex and 6–24 months to first deal. At $8,000 monthly overhead, six months alone consumes $48,000; the $61,000 example needs extension funding or a reduced spending plan.

worksheets.completion_gate: All three canonical scenarios reconcile exactly, fee revenue excludes client recoveries, every modeled cost appears once, and a dated unrestricted cash schedule identifies funded runway and explicit responses to delayed collections.

worksheets.title: Execution, Ledger, and Technical QA Pre-Flight
worksheets.purpose: Convert an accepted mandate into a controlled execution record from intake through satisfaction. Establish document lineage, attorney ownership, deadline review, payment allocation, and exception handling so automation supports the case without inventing authority, balances, court events, or cleared funds.
instructions: Assign a durable matter identifier and preserve original documents separately from working extracts. Record source timestamps, document hashes, access permissions, and reviewer decisions so a balance calculation or enforcement instruction can be traced to its supporting evidence.

Define the matter states and the evidence required for each transition. Route legal decisions to retained counsel and cash decisions to the designated ledger reviewer; an automated status change cannot authorize a levy, settlement, or distribution.

Build a deadline register from the applicable rules and actual docket events, with independent review of anchor dates and calendar treatment. Test amendments, service changes, returned notices, and stays before relying on reminder delivery.

Reconcile bank activity, matter balances, and the aggregate client-money ledger using cleared transactions and explicit allocation rules. Investigate every unmatched item, duplicate reference, reversal, and timing difference before releasing a distribution.

Run the pre-flight tests on synthetic records before processing live matters. Save expected results, observed results, responsible reviewers, and unresolved defects; block affected actions when a test exposes inaccurate balances, missed holds, or incorrect account ownership.

fields.name: Matter identifier and document provenance
fields.prompt: Specify the identifier format, source register, original-file storage, version handling, and review ownership. Explain how extracted data remains linked to source pages and how later corrections preserve the prior audit record.
fields.example: JR-001 stores the entered judgment, lease, docket export, and engagement as separate restricted originals. A SHA-256 digest and retrieval timestamp identify each file. The principal extraction cites judgment page 2; a corrected debtor address creates a new reviewed version instead of replacing the source document.

fields.name: Execution states and transition evidence
fields.prompt: Define operational states from referral through closure, the evidence needed to advance, and who owns each transition. Include explicit paths for bankruptcy, identity mismatch, disputed authority, returned payments, and client-directed termination.
fields.example: The sequence is received, authority verified, counsel reviewed, investigation authorized, enforcement active, payment pending, reconciled, and closed. A bankruptcy signal moves any active case to legal hold. Only counsel's documented disposition permits resumption; cleared payment and ledger review are separately required before a creditor distribution.

fields.name: Attorney enforcement packet
fields.prompt: List the documents and calculations counsel needs before selecting an enforcement remedy. Separate factual research from legal drafting and record the authorized budget, proposed targets, ownership evidence, and unresolved priority concerns.
fields.example: The packet includes the judgment, assignment evidence if applicable, payment ledger, interest worksheet, debtor identifiers, asset sources, and $2,500 spending limit. Counsel selects the lawful remedy and arranges required court and levying-officer steps. The operator does not convert an asset lead into a private instruction to seize property.

fields.name: Deadline register and independent calendar check
fields.prompt: Record each deadline's event, jurisdiction, rule, anchor date, calculation method, responsible attorney, and reminder schedule. Describe how a second reviewer checks the result and how revised orders replace earlier operational reminders.
fields.example: A renewal-review record for JR-001 links the entered judgment to counsel's analysis of California Code of Civil Procedure section 683.020. Internal reminders occur 180, 90, and 30 days before the attorney-approved target. These are operational buffers, not statutory extensions; a second reviewer confirms dates and any intervening renewal.

fields.name: Interest and balance calculation controls
fields.prompt: Specify the applicable rate source, day-count convention, payment allocation sequence, rounding, and treatment of allowed costs. Explain which legal assumptions require review and how the calculator prevents unsupported additions or retroactive rate changes.
fields.example: For the illustrative $120,000 ordinary California commercial money judgment, counsel confirms the 10% rule under Code of Civil Procedure section 685.010 and checks applicable exceptions. Exactly 90 days at simple interest produces $2,958.90. Tests reject added collection charges unless a documented contractual or statutory basis supports inclusion.

fields.name: Matter ledger and three-way reconciliation
fields.prompt: Define the bank control balance, aggregate client liability, individual matter balances, and reconciliation frequency. Explain how the team records fees, distributions, advances, and unresolved receipts without mixing client property with operating funds.
fields.example: A permitted client-money account receives a $40,000 cleared JR-001 payment. Its $40,000 control balance equals the aggregate matter ledger and the single matter balance. After authorized $14,000 fee and $26,000 creditor transfers, all three equal zero. The designated reviewer verifies account requirements and retains both payment confirmations.

fields.name: Receipt matching and duplicate prevention
fields.prompt: Describe the identifiers used to match bank receipts to matters, the handling of partial payments, and the mechanism preventing duplicate posting. Specify how ambiguous references and bank reversals enter an exception queue.
fields.example: The import uses bank transaction ID, account identifier, amount, and posting date as its controlled match record. A repeated import of receipt R-204 for $5,000 creates no second credit. An unreferenced $2,500 receipt remains unallocated pending investigation; the system never guesses a debtor from amount alone.

fields.name: Pre-flight test cases and expected outcomes
fields.prompt: List concrete test inputs and expected outputs for arithmetic, duplicate events, identity mismatches, holds, and payment reversals. Identify which failures block which actions and preserve results without describing unexecuted tests as successful.
fields.example: Test A expects $2,958.90 interest for the 90-day sample. Test B imports R-204 twice and expects one $5,000 posting. Test C places JR-001 on bankruptcy hold and expects every enforcement task to stop. These are acceptance criteria; an execution log must record actual results before production use.

fields.name: Exceptions, disputes, and reversal workflow
fields.prompt: Assign owners and response targets for disputed balances, mistaken identity, reversed funds, and conflicting court information. Explain how the case is contained and how corrected records reach counsel, the creditor, and downstream systems.
fields.example: A $5,000 payment reversal freezes the related fee release and distribution immediately. The ledger reviewer records the reversal, links the original receipt, and informs counsel and the creditor within one business day. If money already left, management funds the required correction without drawing from another client's balance.

fields.name: Satisfaction, release, and archival packet
fields.prompt: Define the evidence required to close a matter after payment, settlement, withdrawal, or exhaustion. Include satisfaction and lien-release responsibilities, remaining balances, final distributions, retention rules, and confirmation that automated outreach has stopped.
fields.example: After settlement performance is verified, counsel determines the required satisfaction filing under California Code of Civil Procedure section 724.010 and related provisions. The closing packet contains the agreement, cleared receipts, final ledger, filing evidence, and required releases. Closure also disables future payment reminders and schedules policy-based record retention.

worksheets.completion_gate: Every active matter has source-linked authority, attorney-owned legal actions, independently checked deadlines, reconciled client balances, and documented test results; unresolved defects block the specific actions they could corrupt.

worksheets.title: Statutory, Licensing, Contract, and Outreach Audit
worksheets.purpose: Determine the actual legal perimeter for each jurisdiction, debt type, data source, and proposed communication. Convert statutory requirements and engagement terms into assigned operating controls, with clear boundaries between commercial recovery support, licensed collection activity, and legal representation.
instructions: Inventory where the operator, creditor, debtor, assets, and communications are located. Have qualified counsel map applicable collection licensing, bonding, local registration, and conduct requirements before assuming that a commercial judgment avoids every collection statute.

Classify the underlying obligation from original transaction evidence rather than debtor labels. Identify any natural-person debtor, household purpose, or mixed-purpose issue that could alter federal or state obligations, and route ambiguous matters for documented review.

Review the engagement, any assignment, counsel retainer, fee calculation, cost authority, and client-money process as one connected package. Remove contradictions about ownership, settlement authority, representation, reimbursement, and who must deliver required filings or notices.

Audit each data source and communication channel against its lawful purpose, access terms, statutory restrictions, and recipient context. Treat creditor acquisition marketing separately from debtor collection communications; permission for one activity does not authorize the other.

Create a dated evidence register with a responsible reviewer for every material requirement. Use specific stop conditions for expired credentials, disputed identity, bankruptcy, protected property, and unauthorized data access, and require documented resolution before affected activity resumes.

fields.name: Jurisdiction and licensing matrix
fields.prompt: Identify the operating jurisdictions and exact activities proposed in each, then record counsel's licensing, bonding, registration, and exemption analysis. Specify evidence and renewal dates rather than relying on a broad commercial-debt label.
fields.example: The pilot involves a California operator, creditor, debtor, and machinery. Counsel evaluates the Debt Collection Licensing Act, California Financial Code section 100000 et seq., including its scope and definitions. The record separately addresses commercial-only activities and local requirements; expansion to another state requires a fresh jurisdiction-specific determination.

fields.name: Federal and state debt classification
fields.prompt: Determine whether the obligation arises primarily from personal, family, household, or business purposes and whether the operator meets applicable collector definitions. Record the supporting transaction documents and consequences for communications and process design.
fields.example: The forklift lease supports a business-purpose classification. Counsel checks 15 U.S.C. section 1692a(5) and (6), Regulation F at 12 CFR Part 1006 when applicable, and California Civil Code section 1788.2. A judgment does not erase the original obligation's consumer character when the underlying transaction was personal.

fields.name: Assignment and representation boundaries
fields.prompt: Explain whether the operator acts as service provider, judgment purchaser, or assignee, and identify who provides legal representation. Address assignment validity, required court records, entity representation, and restrictions on nonlawyer legal activity.
fields.example: The pilot uses a service agreement with the creditor retaining ownership and separately retaining counsel. California Business and Professions Code sections 6125 and 6126 inform the representation boundary. Purchasing a judgment or filing an assignment does not automatically authorize a nonlawyer to represent an entity in court.

fields.name: Bankruptcy stay and discharge controls
fields.prompt: Define the checks and escalation steps for petitions, stay notices, discharge information, and competing insolvency proceedings. State who determines legal effect and how the team prevents prohibited demands, process, or distributions while the issue is reviewed.
fields.example: Any credible bankruptcy notice immediately pauses enforcement and debtor demands on the affected matter. Counsel evaluates 11 U.S.C. sections 362 and 524 and determines permissible next steps. Existing liens, business debt, or an assumed exception do not let an employee restart collection without that documented legal determination.

fields.name: Exemptions and protected-property review
fields.prompt: Identify whose property is targeted, which jurisdiction's protections apply, and what claim or notice procedures must be honored. Distinguish entity property from individual earnings, benefits, and household assets before estimating available value.
fields.example: The LLC machinery analysis does not extend to a guarantor's wages or benefits. For an individual target, counsel reviews applicable California Code of Civil Procedure section 704.010 et seq., 15 U.S.C. section 1673, and relevant benefit protections such as 42 U.S.C. section 407 before selecting process.

fields.name: Lawful data access and vendor terms
fields.prompt: List each research source, authorized purpose, permitted users, retention restriction, and evidence of lawful access. Identify sources requiring a specific permissible purpose and forbid impersonation, borrowed credentials, or unsupported access to personal financial information.
fields.example: Approved sources include court records, Secretary of State registrations, and properly authorized vendor searches. Consumer-report access requires a documented permissible purpose under 15 U.S.C. section 1681b. Motor-vehicle data requires separate analysis under 18 U.S.C. section 2721; obtaining bank information by pretext implicates 15 U.S.C. section 6821.

fields.name: Engagement terms and collection economics
fields.prompt: Record the operative fee clause, cost responsibility, settlement authority, termination rights, reporting obligation, and payment custody arrangement. Identify how counsel reviews fee-sharing or referral issues and resolves inconsistencies between separate agreements.
fields.example: The service agreement states 35% of cleared recoveries, separate written approval for outside costs above $2,500, and creditor control over settlement authorization. Counsel's retainer separately defines legal fees. No nonlawyer payment is calculated as a share of counsel's legal fee without an applicable professional-rules analysis.

fields.name: Debtor communication and channel rules
fields.prompt: Define permitted recipients, identity checks, channel restrictions, represented-party routing, dispute handling, and prohibited statements. Assess calling and texting requirements independently from debt classification, and preserve the approved message and delivery record.
fields.example: A verified business contact receives a factual reference to the entered judgment and counsel's contact details. Staff make no arrest threats or unsupported claims of imminent seizure. Automated calling or texting is disabled until reviewed under 47 U.S.C. section 227 and applicable state rules; represented-party issues route through counsel.

fields.name: Creditor marketing and referral practices
fields.prompt: Distinguish outreach seeking creditor clients from communications collecting debts. Specify truthful performance claims, email identity, opt-out handling, referral compensation review, and the data sources used to identify prospective commercial judgment holders.
fields.example: A creditor prospecting email offers a document-based review rather than promised recovery. Commercial email follows 15 U.S.C. section 7704, including accurate headers, required identification and address information, and functioning opt-out handling. The team suppresses requests operationally within one business day and verifies the statutory outside deadline.

fields.name: Requirement register and stop conditions
fields.prompt: Assign each material requirement an owner, source, review date, evidence artifact, and specific consequence for failure. Explain who can resolve the issue and how that resolution propagates to case tasks and communication systems.
fields.example: The register contains licensing analysis, counsel engagement, approved scripts, vendor authorization, account procedures, and bankruptcy checks. An expired required credential blocks affected new activity; an identity dispute blocks targeting. The responsible reviewer records corrective evidence and the exact permitted resumption scope rather than clearing every restriction at once.

worksheets.completion_gate: Qualified reviewers have documented the jurisdictional and activity-specific requirements, contracts match the actual operating model, lawful data access is evidenced, and every material unresolved issue has a functioning stop condition.

worksheets.title: Automation, Growth Flywheel, and Risk Fallback Tracker
worksheets.purpose: Build a narrow automation system around court deadline tracking and payment reconciliation while keeping legal judgment with qualified people. Connect evidence-based creditor acquisition to capacity, unit economics, exception handling, and tested manual fallbacks rather than maximizing unreviewed outbound volume.
instructions: Diagram the pipeline from approved sources through case intake, attorney review, calendars, ledger, and reporting. Give every transfer an owner, required fields, deduplication rule, permission boundary, and failure destination before connecting production systems.

Prioritize the two canonical automation levers: court deadline tracking and payment reconciliation. Automate extraction, reminders, matching, and exception routing, but require source-linked review before extracted information becomes a legal deadline or distributable balance.

Build creditor outreach from a narrow vertical and a documented lawful source list. Measure qualified referrals, complete packets, accepted mandates, collected fees, and acquisition cost separately so activity volume cannot masquerade as recoverable revenue.

Set capacity limits using actual reviewer hours, active investigations, and attorney availability. Pause new intake when exceptions or legal holds exceed service capacity rather than increasing automated contact to compensate for weak execution.

Exercise a manual fallback for source outages, broken imports, missed reminders, bankruptcy notices, and incorrect matches. Record detection time, containment action, restoration evidence, and backlog ownership before relying on the automation during live matters.

fields.name: System map and permission boundaries
fields.prompt: Identify the selected tools, their data responsibilities, authorized users, and transfer methods. Explain where original evidence lives and which systems may suggest actions without being allowed to execute legal or payment decisions.
fields.example: The pilot uses Microsoft 365 restricted document libraries, an access-controlled case register, Outlook reminders, and accounting exports. PACER and state court records remain external evidence sources. The register can suggest review tasks but cannot file court papers, release money, or override a counsel-entered legal hold.

fields.name: Court source ingestion and provenance
fields.prompt: Specify allowed court sources, retrieval frequency, source identifiers, access terms, and extraction confidence handling. Explain how changed documents, ambiguous names, and incomplete docket coverage reach a human reviewer instead of creating silent updates.
fields.example: A researcher checks active docket sources each business day where access permits, recording court, case, retrieval time, and document link. A changed judgment date creates a review task rather than rewriting calendars. Restricted portals use authorized manual retrieval instead of bypassing access controls.

fields.name: Deadline automation and escalation
fields.prompt: Define the structured deadline fields, independent verification, reminder cadence, delivery monitoring, and escalation path. Explain how a legal hold or amended event changes operational tasks without deleting the historical record.
fields.example: Each deadline stores the source event, attorney-approved date, rule reference, owner, and second reviewer. Reminders at 180, 90, and 30 days feed a daily exception report. A failed delivery alerts the case lead that morning; an amended order supersedes the task while preserving the earlier calculation.

fields.name: Payment automation and exception thresholds
fields.prompt: Define import frequency, matching keys, tolerance, duplicate handling, and review requirements for payment allocation. Describe how the system handles fees, reversals, and client transfers without equating a bank feed with final reconciliation.
fields.example: Daily bank exports match receipts using transaction IDs and approved matter references. The posting tolerance is $0.00: a $4,995 receipt against a $5,000 installment becomes an exception, not an automatic discount. A reviewer confirms cleared funds and three-way reconciliation before any distribution instruction.

fields.name: Creditor acquisition funnel
fields.prompt: Define the target creditor segment, lawful prospect source, outreach sequence, qualification criteria, and measured conversion stages. Keep acquisition metrics separate from debtor contacts, judgment face amounts, and recognized recovery fees.
fields.example: A monthly pilot researches 40 commercial equipment lessors, sends 20 individually reviewed emails, receives six responses, and obtains three complete judgment packets. One accepted mandate is an intake result, not earned revenue. Opt-outs enter a shared suppression list before subsequent campaign preparation.

fields.name: Referral flywheel and service evidence
fields.prompt: Specify the service experience that earns repeat creditor referrals, the reporting cadence, and the evidence used in marketing. Explain how case confidentiality, testimonial permission, and attorney referral restrictions shape the process.
fields.example: Every active creditor receives a monthly report showing verified actions, approved costs, collected amounts, and next evidence requests. After three accurate reporting cycles, the account lead requests an introduction. Case results appear externally only with appropriate permission, and no referral payment is promised before review.

fields.name: Acquisition cost and collected-fee payback
fields.prompt: Calculate acquisition spend per qualified packet and accepted mandate, then estimate payback from earned contribution rather than judgment face value. State timing assumptions and avoid booking expected recoveries as realized returns.
fields.example: A $1,200 monthly prospecting budget yielding three complete packets costs $400 per packet. One accepted mandate costs $1,200. If that matter later produces $10,000 contribution before shared overhead, the acquisition cost consumes 12% of that amount. Until collection, the cash outlay remains unrecovered.

fields.name: Capacity and exception-driven intake limits
fields.prompt: Allocate weekly review hours across intake, active investigations, ledger review, and creditor reporting. State the maximum work in progress and the exception threshold that pauses new acceptances before existing matters deteriorate.
fields.example: The owner allocates 12 weekly hours to underwriting, 10 to case coordination, six to ledger review, and 12 to administration and growth. New acceptances pause above five unresolved payment exceptions or two overdue attorney reviews. Contractor capacity is tracked separately from the owner's 40-hour schedule.

fields.name: Manual fallback and restoration checklist
fields.prompt: Describe the manual operating path for each critical automation failure. Assign detection and restoration owners, preserve pending work, and specify the reconciliation needed before restarting automated imports, reminders, or downstream tasks.
fields.example: If the bank import fails, the ledger reviewer downloads an authorized statement and records receipts in a controlled worksheet. Automated posting remains paused. Restoration requires matching the manual transaction IDs against the recovered feed so the same $5,000 receipt cannot post twice.

fields.name: Risk trigger and fallback owner
fields.prompt: Record the observable triggers for insolvent debtors, bankruptcy stays, and enforcement cost escalation. Pair each with an immediate operational response, decision owner, communication requirement, and evidence needed to resume spending.
fields.example: A bankruptcy notice triggers legal hold and counsel review. Evidence that machinery belongs to an affiliate removes it from the asset pool. A revised $4,000 execution estimate exceeding the $2,500 mandate stops new commitments until the creditor authorizes a revised economics-backed plan.

worksheets.completion_gate: Deadline and reconciliation workflows have named owners, source-linked review, monitored exception queues, and exercised manual fallbacks; growth spending is capped by funded cash and demonstrated execution capacity.

worksheets.title: 30-Day Launch, Pod KPIs, and Exit-Readiness Ledger
worksheets.purpose: Launch a disciplined operating pod without confusing setup progress with collected revenue. Translate the canonical scorecard into staffing, cash, review cadence, and evidence milestones, then preserve the records a future manager or buyer would need to evaluate a transferable business.
instructions: Use the first 30 days to establish a lawful operating perimeter, reliable records, funded runway, and a small qualified pipeline. Keep the canonical six-to-twenty-four-month time to first deal visible; a launch checklist does not accelerate collection by itself.

Assign work to the actual pod rather than an imaginary department structure. Define the owner's full-time responsibilities and each contractor's scope, availability, cost, evidence standards, and escalation path, including separately retained legal representation where required.

Track leading indicators such as complete packets and reviewed asset evidence alongside lagging indicators such as cleared recoveries and earned fees. Use fixed definitions, dated denominators, and source-linked reports to prevent selective success reporting.

Review profitability, unrestricted cash, client-money reconciliation, legal holds, and deadline exceptions on a fixed cadence. Record decisions and owners when a threshold is missed, and defer expansion until the existing pod can support it.

Build exit-readiness continuously through clean contracts, reconciled books, documented workflows, and lawful data handling. Distinguish transferable operating assets from client property, attorney relationships, licenses, and contracts requiring specific consent or replacement.

fields.name: Days 1–7: operating perimeter and funding
fields.prompt: List the first week's deliverables for jurisdiction review, counsel engagement, banking, contract design, data authorization, and capital. Assign an owner and completion evidence for each without treating preparation as permission to start enforcement.
fields.example: By day 7, the owner obtains a written jurisdiction analysis, counsel retainer, reviewed service agreement, account procedures, and a dated cash forecast. The $61,000 opening requirement from Worksheet 2 must be evidenced by available unrestricted funds or intake is constrained to the smaller funded plan.

fields.name: Days 8–14: records and control rehearsal
fields.prompt: Define the second week's case register, document repository, deadline process, ledger configuration, and test deliverables. Identify the evidence showing that staff can detect and contain errors before using live client data.
fields.example: By day 14, synthetic JR-001 records exercise the $120,000 principal, 90-day interest calculation, duplicate $5,000 receipt, and bankruptcy hold. The case lead records observed results and corrective actions. Any incorrect posting blocks live imports until a repeat test demonstrates the specified outcome.

fields.name: Days 15–21: qualified creditor pipeline
fields.prompt: Specify the third week's narrow prospect list, outreach volume, qualification questions, packet requirements, and review budget. Separate permission to market services from authority to contact debtors or pursue their property.
fields.example: By day 21, the research contractor builds 40 documented commercial lessor prospects, and the owner reviews 20 individualized messages. The target is three complete judgment packets, not three recoveries. Each packet needs the judgment, underlying transaction, payment history, and creditor authority before underwriting begins.

fields.name: Days 22–30: controlled acceptance and review
fields.prompt: Define the final week's acceptance criteria, case spending limits, reporting rehearsal, and launch review. State which missing evidence requires deferral and how the team records progress when no fee has yet been earned.
fields.example: By day 30, the pod seeks one fully reviewed mandate with a $750 initial investigation limit and documented counsel ownership. The launch report may show zero recognized revenue and zero recoveries. Missing authority or priority evidence keeps the case deferred rather than being waived to satisfy a launch target.

fields.name: Pod staffing and responsibility ledger
fields.prompt: Assign the canonical staffing to specific operating functions and distinguish employees, contractors, and external vendors. Explain coverage, separation of duties, and the process for buying additional capacity without silently changing the scorecard team.
fields.example: Conservative and Base use 1 FT owner plus 3 C: research, reconciliation support, and outside counsel. The owner reviews contractor-prepared distributions. Scaled uses 2 FT plus 4 C, adding an operations employee and case-support contractor. Court and process-service vendors are purchased services, not hidden full-time positions.

fields.name: Canonical scorecard and positioning
fields.prompt: Record the candidate identity, pipeline rank, Money-to-Manpower score, component scores, and revenue basis. Explain how the rating guides operating design without being presented as a measured probability of collecting a particular judgment.
fields.example: Candidate #8, Judgment Recovery, is pipeline rank #15 of 29 and scores 77/100, a High-Leverage Operator Play. Components are revenue 20, margin 21, team efficiency 16, startup accessibility 10, and automation 10. The revenue basis is recognized service fees, not client asset value or judgment principal.

fields.name: Weekly KPI definitions and exception review
fields.prompt: Define a small scorecard with exact numerators, denominators, measurement dates, and owners. Include pipeline quality, evidence freshness, deadline coverage, payment exceptions, unrestricted cash, and earned fees without combining incompatible periods or populations.
fields.example: Friday review shows three complete packets from six responses, a 50% completion rate; one accepted mandate from three reviewed packets, 33.3%; zero overdue approved deadlines; and two unresolved receipt exceptions. The cash report lists only unrestricted funds, while earned fees remain zero until the contractual recognition event occurs.

fields.name: Monthly economics and expansion decision
fields.prompt: Compare actual fees, costs, profit, and cash to the annual scenario definitions. Explain seasonal or lumpy collections and state the documented conditions for adding capacity rather than extrapolating one favorable month.
fields.example: Base annual fees of $280,000 average $23,333.33 monthly, and $84,000 owner net profit averages $7,000, but receipts need not arrive evenly. Expansion requires funded cash, positive cohort contribution, current reconciliations, and covered legal reviews. The Scaled target remains $500,000 fees and $200,000 annual owner net profit.

fields.name: Exit-readiness and transferable records
fields.prompt: Identify the financial, contractual, operational, and data records needed for a future management transition or sale. Separate owned business assets from client funds and rights requiring consent, new credentials, or replacement agreements.
fields.example: The readiness folder contains monthly fee reconciliations, cohort costs, executed engagements, contractor agreements, workflow versions, and a contract assignment matrix. Client balances are excluded from seller cash. Counsel reviews transfer restrictions, licensing changes, confidentiality, and professional relationships before any buyer receives identifiable case records.

fields.name: Day-30 decision and next funded milestone
fields.prompt: Conclude with a specific continue, constrain, or pause decision based on evidence, cash, and capacity. Record the next milestone, spending ceiling, accountable owner, review date, and conditions that would change the decision.
fields.example: Continue only with verified authority, tested records, current legal review, and the funded cash floor. The next 30 days authorize up to $8,000 recurring overhead and case-specific approved advances. If forecast unrestricted cash falls below $12,000, the owner constrains new intake and resolves funding before further commitments.

worksheets.completion_gate: The day-30 review records actual deliverables, unresolved issues, verified test outcomes, funded runway, staffing ownership, and the next bounded milestone; no mandate, judgment balance, or projected recovery is reported as earned service revenue.
